title: Protection of newborn animals through maternal immunization.
ehr_evidence: This is a narrative review/overview of veterinary maternal vaccination literature; no electronic, individual-level, or routinely collected health data source was analysed.
summary: A narrative review of maternal immunization in domestic animals (cattle, dogs, pigs) to provide neonates with passively transferred immunity against infectious diseases.
key_findings: In a specific pathogen-free model, piglets born to PCV2-vaccinated gilts expressed significantly fewer clinical signs and lesions and had significantly lower viral load in serum, faeces and lymph nodes than piglets born to non-vaccinated gilts.
Field studies reported a significant decrease of post-weaning multisystemic syndrome and global mortality in neonatal and finishing pigs following maternal vaccination.
For the inactivated canine herpesvirus-1 vaccine, vaccination resulted in uniform seroconversion and high neutralizing antibody titres in bitches, with no cases of CHV disease recorded in puppies.
Maternal vaccination enhanced antibody titres in the colostrum and milk of vaccinated cows, with well-established safety and efficacy for pregnant cows and newborn calves.
pathologies_diseases: Neonatal calf diarrhoea/enteritis (E. coli, rotavirus, coronavirus, Cryptosporidium parvum)
Canine herpesvirus-1 (CHV-1) infection and neonatal mortality/abortion
Post-weaning multisystemic syndrome (PWMS) caused by porcine circovirus type 2
population: Newborn animals (calves, puppies, piglets) and their pregnant mothers (cows, bitches, sows)
limitations: Narrative review without primary data analysis or standardized methodology; findings are drawn from cited field and laboratory studies rather than a single analysed dataset.
No environmental or exposome exposure assessment; not applicable to EHR-based human studies.
